title: Intelligence Theories: Spearman, Cattell, Horn, Jensen, Vernon
summary: Two-Factor Theory (Spearman), Fluid and Crystallised Intelligence (Cattell), Gf-Gc theory (Horn), Jensen's Level I/II, Vernon's Hierarchical Model.
objectives: Explain Spearman's Two-Factor Theory (g and s factors).
Describe Jensen's Level I and Level II.
revision: Spearman: g (general) + s (specific). Cattell: Gf (novel reasoning) + Gc (acquired knowledge). Jensen: Level I (associative) + Level II (cognitive). Vernon: g → group factors → minor factors.
traps: g-factor = general intelligence underlying all cognitive abilities.
Fluid = novel problem solving; Crystallised = acquired knowledge.
confusions: Confusing fluid intelligence (declines with age) with crystallised intelligence (stable/increases).

notes.t: Charles Spearman proposed that intelligence consists of a general factor (g) and specific factors (s). The g-factor underlies all cognitive abilities, while s-factors are specific to particular tasks.
Spearman used factor analysis and tetrad differences to demonstrate that correlations among different cognitive tests are positive, suggesting a common underlying factor (g).
The ability to solve novel problems, reason abstractly, and identify patterns independent of acquired knowledge.
The ability to use acquired knowledge, skills, and experience accumulated over a lifetime.
Fluid intelligence tends to decline with age, while crystallised intelligence tends to remain stable or increase.
Jensen's Level I and Level II
Arthur Jensen proposed two levels of intelligence: Level I (associative learning, rote memory) and Level II (cognitive ability, abstract reasoning, problem solving).
Vernon proposed a hierarchical model with g at the top, major group factors (verbal-educational and practical-mechanical) in the middle, and minor group factors at the bottom.
UGC NET frequently asks about Spearman's g-factor, Cattell's Gf-Gc distinction, and Vernon's hierarchical model.
